description: Flutter mobile app starter — Dart 3, Material 3, GoRouter-based navigation, Provider state management, Dio HTTP client. For products that want a single Dart codebase shipping to iOS, Android, web, and desktop with Google's first-party mobile framework (not React Native / Expo).

defaults.headline: Starter Foundry Flutter App
defaults.subheadline: A Flutter mobile shell with GoRouter nav, Provider state, and Dio networking wired for auth, billing, and wallet seams.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick flutter-app when the user names Flutter, Dart, pubspec, GoRouter, Provider, Riverpod, BLoC, Cupertino, or Material 3 — Google's first-party SDK with a single Dart codebase shipping to iOS + Android + web + desktop. For JS/TS-driven React Native workflows use expo-react-native-ts. For iOS-only Swift use swiftui-expo. For Kotlin-first multiplatform with Compose UI use kotlin-multiplatform.
firstSteps: Run `flutter pub get` to resolve pubspec.yaml dependencies
Run `flutter run` to launch on a connected device or simulator
Edit lib/main.dart to add new screens; register routes in the GoRouter config
Use Provider (or swap to Riverpod) for app-wide state — see the ChangeNotifier example in lib/main.dart
gotchas: Flutter requires the Flutter SDK locally — CI and scaffold validation only check structure, not compile. Run `flutter analyze` before shipping.
iOS builds need Xcode + a provisioning profile; Android needs JDK 17+ and the Android SDK. Don't expect `flutter run` to work in a bare container.
GoRouter 14+ uses declarative routes — mutating route state mid-navigation throws. Always navigate via `context.go(...)` or `context.push(...)`.
Provider rebuilds the entire subtree on notifyListeners — use `Consumer` + `Selector` to scope rebuilds on hot lists.
Dio interceptors run in registration order; auth-refresh interceptors must be added BEFORE logging interceptors or refresh storms show up in logs.
architectureNotes: lib/main.dart wires MaterialApp.router to a GoRouter instance and a MultiProvider root — the two extension seams are (a) new route defs and (b) new ChangeNotifier providers.
Screens live under lib/screens/, services (API clients, repositories) under lib/services/. Keep widgets leaf-only; push state up to providers.

Auth/payments/sdk slots drop config JSON at the project root — a bootstrap hook reads those at app start and rehydrates the matching service. Keep secrets out of the client bundle; fetch from a secured backend.
